text:
Dear Dr. Henderson,

Thank you for evaluating Ms. Karen Davis, a 44-year-old project manager whom I am referring for an opinion on persistent cytopenias that developed earlier this year in adulthood. 

On review of systems, she feels well and denies constitutional symptoms. There has been no excessive bleeding, petechiae, or history of nosebleeds. Her past medical history is non-contributory; she takes only an over-the-counter multivitamin and has no family history of hematologic disorders. Physical examination was unremarkable, with a blood pressure of 118/74 mmHg, clear breath sounds, and no evidence of organomegaly or lymphadenopathy.

Her routine laboratory workup has shown an isolated subnormal platelet count, consistently fluctuating between 55,000 and 70,000 per microliter. Her automated MPV is elevated at 14.2 fL. The peripheral blood smear confirmed significant variation in the size of her circulating platelets, displaying a mix of markedly enlarged forms alongside typical elements. Platelet aggregometry was performed, and in vitro aggregation responses across all standard agonists were completely preserved. Furthermore, a recent marrow aspirate revealed active trilineage hematopoiesis, with marrow megakaryocytes exhibiting normal structural features and appearance.

I would appreciate your consultation regarding these findings and guidance on whether any specialized monitoring or further evaluation is indicated.

Sincerely,
Dr. Arthur Pendelton
